Today's big story: Anthropic Broke Its $83 IPO Price. What Did Facebook Do Next?

Palantir Technologies sits in a group of five large technology companies with Microsoft, Amazon.com, Alphabet and International Business Machines. It has the highest price-to-earnings ratio of the five and the fastest revenue growth, yet its stock came only third over the past year. So is the fastest grower worth picking over the others at its price?

How does Palantir's price compare with what it delivers?

The clearest contrast is with Microsoft. Both keep a similar share of sales as operating profit, 45.6% at Palantir and 47.1% at Microsoft over their latest four reported quarters. But Palantir's shares cost 107.3 times its past year's profit, against 25.5 times for Microsoft. Part of Palantir's profit came from outside its main business. Its $3.67 billion of net income topped its $3.33 billion of operating income.

What the higher price buys is growth. Palantir's revenue rose 87.1% from the four quarters before, while Microsoft's rose 17.9%. The other three rivals also have both a lower price-to-earnings ratio and slower growth. The table below sets out all five.

That lead has not reached the stock. Palantir returned 0.8% over the past year, and its $163.59 close on Wednesday sat well below its $209.05 close on October 9.

Palantir's stock closed at $163.59 on Wednesday, well below its October 9 high, and the company hands its owners no cash while they wait. If you live off your savings, a drop like this can force you to sell shares at a low point. Where is Palantir's growth coming from?

Growth has sped up in each of the past four quarters. Revenue rose 70% from a year earlier in the quarter ended December 2025, then 84.7% in the March quarter and 92.8% in the June quarter. In the quarter ended September 2026 it rose 95.9%. Management said U.S. revenue, most of the total, grew 119% that quarter.

title: Western Digital vs. IBM: Which Data Storage Stock is the Smarter Bet?
detail:
Western Digital vs. IBM: Which Data Storage Stock is the Smarter Bet?
Shreya Majumder
Fri, November 27, 2026 at 4:12 AM PST 7 min read
IBM
WDC
SNDK
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The growing demand for AI, cloud computing, enterprise infrastructure and data centers is creating lucrative opportunities for the global data storage industry. As businesses generate and process increasingly large volumes of information, demand for reliable, high-capacity storage solutions is becoming more essential. Two companies that offer exposure to this market are Western Digital Corporation WDC and International Business Machines Corporation IBM.

However, the companies have considerably different business models. Western Digital has transformed its business focus following the separation of its flash business into Sandisk SNDK in 2025. It is now primarily focused on HDD technology, particularly high-capacity drives used in cloud data centers and enterprise storage environments. IBM offers a different investment proposition, operating across enterprise software, hybrid cloud, consulting, AI and infrastructure. Its storage business includes enterprise storage systems and solutions designed to help organizations manage, protect and access critical information.

So, which stock offers a better investment opportunity? Let's compare their growth prospects, competitive advantages, financial profiles and risks.

The Case for WDC Stock

Western Digital's first-quarter fiscal 2027 results show strong business momentum, with revenue rising 55% year over year to $4.4 billion. Gross margin reached 58.1%, while operating margin was 49.1%. EPS came in at $4.64, and free cash flow totaled $1.4 billion. For the fiscal second quarter, the company expects revenue of $5.1 billion and EPS of $5.80. Demand remains strong across cloud, hyperscale, enterprise, neocloud and AI markets, with HDDs playing a critical role in cost-effective data storage. WD's seven largest customers provide demand visibility through 2030–2031, while growing AI workloads, video storage and physical AI applications offer additional growth opportunities.

Western Digital is advancing its capacity roadmap through 40TB ePMR drives and next-generation HAMR technology. ePMR products are expected to account for 50% of nearline shipments by the fiscal second quarter. It targets completion of HAMR qualifications, followed by volume shipments in the first half of fiscal 2027. The company expects nearline exabyte growth to exceed its long-term target of 25% as these technologies ramp. Pricing and margins remain favorable, with average selling price per terabyte increasing 28% year over year. WDC expects further year-over-year pricing gains over the next three to four quarters, supported by higher-capacity drives and customer agreements.

Chicago, IL – November 27, 2026 – Zacks Equity Research shares Kyndryl Holdings KD as the Bull of the Day and Hermès International HESAY asthe Bear of the Day. In addition, Zacks Equity Research provides analysis on American Airlines AAL, Southwest Airlines LUV and Delta Air Lines DAL.

Here is a synopsis of all five stocks:

Bull of the Day:

Shares of Kyndryl Holdings, a 2021 IBM spinoff, have held up well amid the broader tech selloff as investors respond to improving profitability.

At around $16 a share, KD stock still looks attractively valued after climbing more than 20% since reporting strong results for its fiscal second quarter earlier this month.

What Does Kyndryl Do?

Kyndryl manages the IT infrastructure that large organizations rely on for day-to-day operations, from mainframes and data centers to hybrid cloud environments. Through Kyndryl Consult, it also helps clients modernize applications, strengthen cybersecurity, and put AI to work in existing systems.

Kyndryl's Earnings Outlook Is Improving

Fiscal Q2 showed how Kyndryl can grow earnings even when sales soften. Revenue fell nearly 2% year over year to $3.65 billion, but adjusted pretax income climbed 22% to $150 million and Q2 adjusted EPS rose to $0.42 from $0.38. Furthermore, Kyndryl exceeded Q2 sales and EPS expectations of $3.6 billion and $0.37 per share by over 1% and 13%, respectively.

This comes as analysts still expect annual sales to remain above $14 billion through fiscal 2029. The Zacks Consensus Estimate calls for Kyndryl's EPS to rise 33% to $1.94 in its current FY27 and another 26% to $2.45 in FY28.

Reassuringly, over the past 30 days, FY27 and FY28 EPS estimates have risen more than 4%. Near-term estimates have also risen, with the Q3 EPS consensus up to $0.80 from $0.76 in the last month and the Q4 EPS estimate up to $0.82 from $0.80.

KD's Enticing Valuation

At current levels, KD shares trade at just 8X forward earnings and at less than 1X forward sales. Those are attractive multiples for a tech stock with double-digit earnings growth projected for fiscal 2027 and 2028, offering a more than 50% discount to the forward P/E averages of the benchmark S&P 500 and its Zacks Technology Services Industry. 

Bottom Line

In addition to sporting a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), Kyndryl Holdings stock checks an overall "A" VGM Zacks Style Scores grade for its combination of Value, Growth, and Momentum.

Although KD would be an ideal buy-the-dip target amid broader market weakness, rising earnings estimates and a modest valuation suggest there could still be meaningful upside from here.

International Business Machines (NYSE:IBM) shares climbed 3.33% to $243.47 at the 4:00 p.m. ET close on November 25, after Wedbush started coverage with an Outperform rating and a $276 price target. The gain came against a 0.62% drop in the Nasdaq Composite. Shares opened at $233.50 and traded near $245.25 in the afternoon, up about 5% from the open at that point.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 8 Warning Signs with SOBKY.

Wedbush's Moshe Katri set the new marker after a third quarter in which IBM beat expectations on both lines. Adjusted earnings came in at $2.95 a share against $2.85 expected, and revenue reached $17.10 billion against $16.82 billion. The timing helped. On a day when investors dumped AI hardware names over spending fears, IBM's mix of software, consulting and mainframes may have looked like a way to own AI demand without funding a data center buildout.

The $276 target sits 13.4% above the close, a reasonable gap for a mature company rather than a growth bet. The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 79/100, with steady profitability and momentum held back by a balance sheet that ranks only middling. GF Value is $248.84, a 2.2% discount, and GuruFocus rates the shares fairly valued, so the rally has closed most of the model's gap and leaves little cushion. The next test is fourth-quarter software growth in January, which will show whether IBM's AI bookings turn into revenue fast enough to justify the higher price.
